questions.q: Who makes the determination that a security incident is "material," according to this lesson?
options: Whichever analyst first detected the incident
The organization's cyber insurance carrier
A joint legal judgment made by the CISO, legal and privacy counsel, and typically a disclosure committee — never the security team alone based on technical severity
An automated scoring tool based solely on CVSS
questions.explain: Materiality is a securities-law standard, not a technical severity measure, and is determined jointly by legal, privacy counsel, the CISO, and typically a disclosure committee.

questions.q: What is the legal standard for materiality referenced in this lesson, originating from TSC Industries v. Northway?
options: Whether there is a substantial likelihood a reasonable investor would consider the information important to the total mix of available information
Whether the incident involved more than 10,000 affected records
Whether the CVSS score of the underlying vulnerability exceeds 9.0
Whether the incident was reported by a government agency
questions.explain: Materiality asks whether a reasonable investor would consider the information important to the total mix of information available — a legal test, independent of technical severity or record counts.

questions.q: Under the SEC's cybersecurity disclosure rules, when does the four-business-day clock for a Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing actually start?
options: From the moment any employee first notices unusual activity
From the date the vulnerability was originally patched
From the end of the current fiscal quarter
From the company's determination that the incident is material — not from the initial discovery of the incident
questions.explain: The four-business-day clock runs from the materiality determination, which is why having a disclosure committee and escalation chain ready in advance is critical — delaying that determination doesn't stop the clock from eventually needing to run.

questions.q: What does Form 10-K, Item 106 of Regulation S-K require public companies to disclose annually?
options: A list of every individual employee's security training completion record
Their processes for assessing, identifying, and managing material cybersecurity risks, plus the board's oversight role and management's role and expertise
The full technical architecture of their security operations center
The source code of all internally developed security tools
questions.explain: Item 106 is the SEC's annual disclosure requirement, covering cyber risk management processes and governance — the board's oversight and management's expertise — not technical implementation detail.

questions.q: Why does this lesson distinguish SEC disclosure obligations from state data-breach notification laws and GDPR?
options: Because state and GDPR laws were fully repealed once the SEC rules took effect
Because only one of the three can ever legally apply to a single incident
Because they are identical requirements filed on the same form

Because they are separate, parallel obligations that trigger on different tests and different clocks — breach notification laws protect individuals and trigger on data exposure, while SEC disclosure protects investors and triggers on materiality
questions.explain: The same incident can trigger SEC disclosure, state breach notification, and GDPR's 72-hour authority notification simultaneously, each on its own clock and its own trigger — which is why legal counsel owns determining which apply.
